---
title: Meetings, proposals, and the shape of voice
---

# Introduction

Junior members in organizational meetings are usually described by how much they
speak. This study asks a different question: which proposals are taken up in
later meetings, and which quietly disappear.

Three constructs organize the analysis. [Proposal uptake](research/glossary.md#proposal-uptake)
is the extent to which a proposal made in one meeting becomes a topic of work in
a later one. [Dissent](research/glossary.md#dissent) is an utterance that names a
disagreement with a decision the group had already taken. Both differ from
[felt safety](research/glossary.md#felt-safety), a participant's reported
expectation that raising a concern will not expose them to interpersonal harm.

The fourth construct, speaking frequency, records how often a participant
speaks and says nothing about what the group did with what was said.
<!-- constructs: speaking-frequency -->

The verbatim transcripts are deposited under the
[project record](https://osf.example/registrations/uptake-2026).

The turn count was applied with one rule and no reading of what was said:

```text
uptake = 1 if a later meeting revisits the proposal, else 0
```
